question: On plain 4% up days, does the stock's own volatility (adr20, average daily range %) grade the day? Unlike on burst (where adr20 was a mechanical control since burst events are volatility-gated by construction), this cohort has no such gating, so a real relationship (direction unclear a priori) can show up if base/volatility quality matters generically.
plain: Idea: does how volatile a stock normally is (its average daily range) change how well a plain 4% up day performs, once we are not already filtering for tight bases?
